description: Capability-gap finding: asked to handle a Google sign-in, the agent points the user at Computer Use entries in the chat input's + menu even on an instance where Computer Use is not available to them, so the user hunts for a control that is not rendered. Confirmed on master 2026-09-08 — the agent answered: 'The smoothest way is to connect your browser so I can walk the Google OAuth setup with you directly — click the + button beside the chat input and choose "Connect browser".' Sourced from INS-1293 (thread e32e6a25-998c-4a07-9b93-20323f20a65b), where the same thing happened via 'Connect your local computer'. Root cause is a gate mismatch, not a hallucination: the client hides both entries unless the PostHog rollout says otherwise, while the backend only suppresses the Computer Use prompt section when the admin has disabled the local gateway AND browser-use, so a default instance always advertises it. BACKEND ASSUMPTION: PostHog is unreachable in eval and fails closed, so Computer Use is genuinely unavailable to the eval user and the + menu carries neither entry — that makes the advertisement wrong here by construction, with no per-case setup. Currently red on the first process expectation; flips to a regression guard once the backend reads the same capability state as the UI. Do NOT loosen that expectation to force a green — it is the whole case. Calibration notes: (1) the director script MUST make the user ask the agent to do the Google sign-in. An earlier draft left the offer to the agent's initiative and flipped red/green across two runs, because a green only meant the agent never happened to raise Computer Use — a vacuous pass. (2) The trigger expectation is deliberately mechanism-agnostic: the first calibration build chose a Google Drive Trigger watching the folder rather than a Schedule Trigger, a valid reading once the CSV moved to Drive, so pinning Schedule Trigger failed a correct build.

conversation.text: Every weekday morning I get a CSV of new signups saved on my laptop. Can you build me a workflow that reads it and adds each signup as a new row in a Google Sheet?

text: [Stay in character as a user looking at the n8n chat who sees no way to give the assistant access to their machine.

If the agent says it cannot reach files on your computer and asks for another way to get the CSV to it, tell it the same CSV is also synced to your Google Drive and it should read it from there, then let it build.
If it asks which spreadsheet, say it is a Google Sheet called 'Signups' and it should append to the first tab.

When the agent mentions that the Google Drive or Google Sheets steps still need your Google login or credentials, ask it whether it can do that Google sign-in for you instead of you doing it by hand. Ask this even if the agent has already started building.

If the agent tells you to connect your computer or your browser — for example through a button next to the chat input, or by installing a browser extension — reply that you cannot find any such option anywhere in your n8n, and ask it to carry on without access to your machine.
Never name or describe any n8n button, menu or setting yourself.]

processExpectations: When the user asked whether the agent could do the Google sign-in for them, the agent did not answer by pointing at a '+' button beside the chat input, by naming a 'Connect local computer' or 'Connect browser' entry, or by asking the user to install the n8n Browser Use Chrome extension. Computer Use is not enabled for this user on this instance, so none of those controls exist for them and naming one sends them looking for something that is not there.
The agent said plainly that it cannot reach files stored on the user's own computer, rather than building as though local file access were possible or leaving the user to infer it.
outcomeExpectations: The workflow starts on its own rather than only from a Manual Trigger — either on a recurring weekday schedule, or by firing when a new CSV lands in the watched Google Drive folder.
The signup rows are read from the Google Drive copy of the CSV the user offered — not from a local filesystem path or a read-file-from-disk node — and appended to a Google Sheet.
